_note: Plain-language definitions shown once, at first use, in the Executive Summary details (and as hover titles). Keep each under 12 words.
port scan: probing many ports to find which services are listening
SYN: the first packet of a TCP connection attempt
cleartext: sent without encryption, so anyone on the network can read it
SQL injection: tampering with a database query through user input
XSS: injecting script that runs in other users' browsers
path traversal: using ../ sequences to read files outside the web folder
web shell: a script on a web server that gives remote control
brute force: guessing passwords repeatedly until one works
encoded PowerShell: PowerShell commands hidden in Base64 to avoid inspection
execution policy: a Windows setting that limits which scripts may run
download cradle: a one-line command that downloads and runs a script
reverse shell: a connection from a victim back to the attacker for remote control
C2: command and control: the channel an attacker uses to steer malware
kill chain: the ordered stages an attack moves through
SPF: a DNS record listing servers allowed to send for a domain
DKIM: a cryptographic signature proving the sending domain
DMARC: a domain policy that checks SPF and DKIM alignment
Return-Path: the hidden envelope address that receives bounces
Reply-To: the address replies go to, which can differ from the sender
double extension: a file name like invoice.pdf.exe that hides the real type
URL shortener: a service that hides the real link behind a short one
lookalike: a domain spelled to resemble a trusted brand
reputation: what threat-intelligence services have recorded about an indicator
NSE: Nmap Scripting Engine checks that test services for known issues
banner: the version text a service announces when you connect
end-of-life: no longer receiving security updates from the vendor
DNS tunnelling: hiding data inside DNS lookups to sneak it out
user agent: the client name a browser or tool sends with each request
IOC: indicator of compromise: an IP, domain, hash or URL tied to an attack
